name: Godot
description: An open-source engine with dedicated 2D and 3D workflows.
note: Console exports require third-party porting arrangements. Web export capabilities depend on the language and renderer.

name: Unity
description: A versatile engine with an extensive ecosystem for 2D, 3D, and mobile games.
note: Eligibility and paid-tier requirements depend on current Unity terms. Console builds require approval and export access.

name: Unreal Engine
description: High-fidelity 3D worlds, powerful tooling, and visual scripting.
note: No first-party HTML5 export is cataloged. Royalty obligations and console access depend on current terms.

name: GameMaker
description: A focused 2D engine for fast iteration and polished sprite-based games.
note: Commercial and console licenses have additional terms.

name: GDevelop
description: Build 2D games with a visual event system and no-code workflows.
note: This curated entry focuses on its established 2D workflow, rather than newer 3D capabilities.

name: Phaser
description: A JavaScript and TypeScript framework built for 2D browser games.
note: Native mobile and desktop distribution require additional packaging; only direct browser support is cataloged.

name: GDScript
description: Godot’s integrated scripting language, designed for gameplay iteration.

name: C#
description: A strongly typed language for Unity, Godot .NET, and MonoGame projects.
note: Godot C# export support varies by target; verify its current platform limitations.

name: C++
description: Native gameplay and systems programming for Unreal, SFML, and C-compatible libraries.
note: Unreal and SFML use C++ directly; raylib and SDL expose C APIs usable from C++.

name: Blueprints
description: Unreal’s node-based visual scripting for gameplay and rapid iteration.

name: GML
description: GameMaker’s built-in language for 2D gameplay and tools.

name: Visual events
description: Create game logic through GDevelop’s event system.

name: TypeScript
description: Typed JavaScript for browser games and tooling.

name: VS Code
description: An extensible editor for code, debugging, and project tooling.

name: Blender
description: Model, sculpt, texture, and render your 3D assets.

name: Aseprite
description: A focused editor for pixel art, sprites, and frame animation.

name: Krita
description: Open-source painting for concept art, textures, and illustrations.

name: Photoshop
description: Professional image editing, painting, and texture workflows.

name: Substance 3D Painter
description: Author detailed materials and paint directly on 3D models.

name: Blender animation
description: Rig and animate characters using Blender’s animation toolkit.

name: Engine animation
description: Start with built-in timelines, animation graphs, or sprite playback.
note: Available capabilities vary by engine; this represents a workflow, not a separate product.

name: Spine
description: Create skeletal 2D animation with engine-specific runtimes.
note: Check the runtime integration and license for your selected engine.

name: Maya
description: Studio modeling, character rigging, and animation workflows.

name: Audacity
description: Record, trim, clean, and edit game sound effects.

name: REAPER
description: Produce music and layered sound effects in a full audio workstation.

name: FMOD
description: Adaptive audio middleware with Unity and Unreal integrations.
note: Check current licensing; qualifying projects may have a free license.

name: Wwise
description: Interactive audio authoring and runtime integration for game teams.
note: Integration and licensing depend on engine, platform, and project.

name: Godot multiplayer
description: High-level multiplayer APIs for Godot game sessions.

name: Netcode for GameObjects
description: Unity’s high-level networking package for GameObject workflows.

name: Unreal replication
description: Unreal’s built-in replicated actors and multiplayer networking.

name: Photon Fusion
description: Hosted networking and simulation tooling with a Unity SDK.

name: Nakama
description: Open-source player accounts, social features, and game backend services.

name: PlayFab
description: Managed player data, live operations, and game backend services.

name: Supabase
description: Postgres, authentication, and storage for supporting player services.
note: General-purpose backend; gameplay integration and security require project-specific implementation.

name: Git LFS
description: Version source code with pointers to large binary game assets.

name: Perforce P4
description: Centralized source control suited to large binary asset pipelines.
note: Small-team free options may be available; verify current limits.

name: GitHub
description: Host repositories, review changes, and track development issues.

name: Trello
description: Simple boards for milestones, bugs, and production tasks.

name: Jira
description: Track cross-discipline production work and larger team backlogs.

name: Notion
description: Keep your game design documents and project notes together.

name: Discord
description: Coordinate playtests and communicate with your team or community.

name: GUT
description: A Godot unit-testing framework for GDScript projects.

name: Unity Test Framework
description: Run edit-mode and play-mode tests for Unity projects.

name: Unreal automation
description: Use Unreal’s automation framework to verify gameplay and engine behavior.

name: Playwright
description: Automate browser gameplay checks for web-based games.

name: GitHub Actions
description: Automate checks and supported game builds in CI.
note: Engine licensing, SDK access, build runners, and usage limits still apply.

name: itch.io
description: Share desktop games and supported HTML5 builds with your audience.

name: Steam
description: Commercial desktop distribution with community and platform services.

name: Google Play
description: Distribute Android games through Google’s app marketplace.

name: App Store
description: Distribute iOS games through Apple’s developer ecosystem.

name: Bevy
description: A code-first Rust engine with ECS-based 2D and 3D workflows.
note: A Rust and Cargo workflow. Verify renderer support, platform setup, and version migration requirements for your project.

name: SFML
description: A C++ multimedia library for 2D graphics, windows, audio, and input.
note: A multimedia library, not a scene editor. Mobile support has additional setup and experimental caveats. Browser output and a complete 3D renderer are not verified here.

name: raylib
description: A small C library for programming 2D and 3D games, with many language bindings.
note: Native C/C++ plus bindings such as Odin. Verified mobile output here is Android; iOS requires a separate porting route. Binding and browser-build support must be checked together.

name: SDL3
description: Low-level C tooling for windows, input, audio, and a custom rendering pipeline.
note: A foundation for your own engine, not a complete game editor. Browser builds use Emscripten; 3D requires a separate renderer. Additional SDL libraries handle fonts and image formats.

name: LÖVE
description: A lightweight Lua framework for 2D games and rapid code-driven iteration.
note: Write your game loop and integrations in Lua. Browser builds require a separate community runtime and are not cataloged as direct support.

name: MonoGame
description: A C# game framework for custom 2D and 3D games with a content pipeline.
note: A framework rather than a visual scene editor. Console packages require registered-developer access. Direct browser builds are not verified in this catalog.

name: Defold
description: A compact cross-platform engine with an editor and Lua gameplay scripting.
note: Uses the Defold license rather than an OSI open-source license. Console access has approval and platform-specific terms; verify the target and asset workflow.

name: Rust
description: A systems language for Bevy gameplay and memory-safe native tooling.
note: Bevy uses Rust directly. Other game-library bindings have their own integration and platform support.

name: C
description: Native programming for raylib, SDL3, and custom game engines.

name: Odin
description: A data-oriented systems language with bundled raylib and SDL bindings.
note: Odin ships vendor bindings for raylib and SDL3. Confirm the binding version, linking setup, and cross-compilation route for your targets.

name: Lua
description: A lightweight scripting language used by LÖVE and Defold.

name: Tiled
description: Build tile maps and object layers in a flexible 2D level editor.
note: Choose a loader or importer matching your engine and exported map format.

name: LDtk
description: A focused 2D level editor with auto-tiling and entity-oriented workflows.
note: JSON output needs a compatible importer or a custom loading implementation.

name: Krita animation
description: Author frame-by-frame 2D animation and export assets for your runtime.
note: Animation authoring is separate from runtime sprite playback. Export and load frames using your chosen library or framework.

name: Cargo
description: Build Rust projects, resolve packages, and run Rust unit and integration tests.
note: Cargo tests cover Rust logic; graphics and platform integration still need suitable runtime tests.

name: CMake
description: Configure and generate native C and C++ build systems.

name: Catch2
description: A native C++ framework for unit tests and gameplay-logic checks.
note: Requires a C++ test target. A C or Odin game does not directly use Catch2 without a C++ bridge.

name: .NET testing
description: Run C# gameplay-logic tests using dotnet test and a selected test framework.
note: Choose a compatible test framework. Engine lifecycle and rendering checks need additional runtime coverage.

name: Odin testing
description: Run Odin test procedures through the compiler’s test command.
note: Tests use Odin procedures and core:testing; no C++ test framework is required.

name: RenderDoc
description: Inspect supported native graphics API frame captures and rendering state.
note: Check the graphics API and host platform first; this is not a universal browser or Metal graphics debugger.

name: Tracy
description: Instrument CPU work, allocations, and supported GPU workloads for profiling.
note: Requires instrumentation and an integration matching your language, engine, and target.
